items.stem: For a resistor obeying Ohm's law, if the voltage across it doubles while resistance is constant, the current through it:

options.rationale: Correct: I = V/R, so with R fixed, doubling V doubles I.
Current rises with voltage when resistance is fixed; it does not fall.
With R fixed, current is proportional to voltage, so it changes.
Ohm's law is linear, so current scales by the same factor as voltage.

items.explanation: Correct: I = V/R, so with R fixed, doubling V doubles I.

items.stem: A net force acts on a body of constant mass. According to Newton's second law, the body's acceleration is:

options.text: Directly proportional to the net force
options.rationale: Correct: a = F/m, so acceleration scales with net force at constant mass.

options.text: Inversely proportional to the net force
options.rationale: Acceleration rises, not falls, with net force.
Newton's second law ties acceleration directly to net force.

options.text: Zero whenever a force is applied
options.rationale: A nonzero net force produces a nonzero acceleration.

items.explanation: Correct: a = F/m, so acceleration scales with net force at constant mass.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about an ideal gas are correct?

options.text: At fixed temperature, pressure and volume are inversely related
options.rationale: Correct: this is Boyle's law, PV = constant at fixed T and n.

options.text: At fixed pressure, volume is proportional to absolute temperature
options.rationale: Correct: this is Charles's law using absolute temperature.
Ideal-gas law uses absolute pressure, not gauge.

options.text: Ideal-gas calculations use Celsius temperature directly
options.rationale: They require absolute (Kelvin or Rankine) temperature.

options.text: An ideal gas has strong intermolecular attractive forces
options.rationale: The ideal-gas model assumes negligible intermolecular forces.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: this is Boyle's law, PV = constant at fixed T and n. Correct: this is Charles's law using absolute temperature.
